title: Getting started with bgnormR
text: bgnorm (Kharbanda, Tubelleza et al. 2025) generative statistical framework background correction, normalisation, quality control multiplex spatial proteomics data, including data Akoya PhenoCycler-Fusion (formerly CODEX), Cell DIVE, IMC, CosMx platforms. framework models log2-transformed fluorescence intensities three-component Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM): Three-component signal model: pixel intensity X sum independent latent sources U1 (background), U2 (non-specific), U3 (signal). closed-form deconvolution step isolates signal component background sources. optional quantile normalisation step (bgnormQ) unifies dynamic range across markers, samples, 3-D tissue slices, enabling single fixed positivity threshold across dataset. Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) components 2 3 provides automated quality control metric: higher JSD indicates better staining quality.

title: Getting started with bgnormR
text: bgnorm_pixels() fits three-component GMM channel independently. sample_prop controls fraction non-zero pixels used fitting — default 0.1 (10 %) sufficient full-resolution Akoya images keeping runtime short. res QPTIFFImage whose pixel values background-adjusted log2-intensities. Per-channel model parameters stored attribute retrieved bgnorm_results(): summary() shows full component table:
code: res <- bgnorm_pixels(img, sample_prop = 0.1) res #> QPTIFFImage #>   Dimensions: 550 x 800 (H x W) #>   Channels  : 5  #>   Names     : CD20, CD3e, CD8, PanCK, Vimentin   #>   Format    : unknown  #>   Levels    : 1  #>   bgnorm    : yes (5 channel(s)) br_panck <- bgnorm_results(res)[["PanCK"]] print(br_panck) #> BgnormResult (pixel-level) #>   n = 440000  #>   Component means: 0.03 0.161 1.884  #>   JSD (QC metric): 0.8811  #>   BIC (G=2): -1.67   BIC (G=3): -1.38  #>   No signal detected: FALSE  #>   Quantile normalised: FALSE  #>   Tissue positivity: 67% summary(br_panck) #> BgnormResult summary (pixel-level) #>   JSD: 0.8811  #>   Quantile normalised: FALSE  #>  #>     component   mean     sd proportion #>    Background 0.0299 0.0186     0.2378 #>  Non-specific 0.1606 0.0897     0.2512 #>        Signal 1.8837 0.9511     0.5110

title: Getting started with bgnormR
text: bgnorm_sce() processes SummarizedExperiment (subclass SingleCellExperiment SpatialExperiment): reads requested assay, runs bgnorm_cells() independently marker, stores adjusted intensities new assay alongside per-marker BgnormResult objects metadata(). Per-marker model parameters accessible via metadata():
code: library(SummarizedExperiment) set.seed(5)  n_cells   <- 200L n_markers <- 5L marker_names <- c("CD20", "CD3e", "CD8", "PanCK", "Vimentin")  make_cell_raw <- function(j) {     inv_log_transform(         c(rnorm(round(n_cells * 0.7), 3, 0.5 + 0.1 * j),           rnorm(round(n_cells * 0.3), 7, 0.8 + 0.1 * j)),         cofactor = 150     ) } raw_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_markers), make_cell_raw)) rownames(raw_mat) <- marker_names colnames(raw_mat) <- paste0("cell", seq_len(n_cells))  se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = raw_mat)) se <- bgnorm_sce(se, assay.type = "counts", name = "bgnorm") assayNames(se) #> [1] "counts" "bgnorm" bgnorm_meta <- S4Vectors::metadata(se)$bgnorm_results cat("JSD for CD20:", round(bgnorm_meta$CD20$jsd, 3), "\n") #> JSD for CD20: 0.989

title: bgnormR 0.99.0
text: Added bgnorm_pixels() pixel-level background normalisation QPTIFFImage objects, supporting parallel channel processing via BiocParallel. Added unified plotting functions: plot_qptiff(), plot_pixel_classes(), plot_distributions(), plot_jsd_heatmap() supporting QPTIFFImage (raster) SpatialExperiment (scatter) input.
